name: Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Durustawayh al-Fārisī
summary: Baghdad grammarian of Persian origin, a student of al-Mubarrad, who defended the Basrans against the Kufans and wrote a book on the writing of Arabic.
bio: Ibn Durustawayh came from Fasā in Fārs and learnt in Baghdad from al-Mubarrad and Ibn Qutayba; al-Zubaydī places him in the ninth Basran generation. He was a sharp partisan of the Basrans and is said to have written against the Kufan views of Thaʿlab's circle.
His Kitāb al-Kuttāb, on spelling and writing, and his Taṣḥīḥ al-faṣīḥ, a commentary on Thaʿlab's al-Faṣīḥ that often corrects it, survive. He died in Baghdad in 347/958.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 43 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
